root_cause.text: The PMBus hwmon regulator support called into shared PMBus register/data paths from `pmbus_regulator_get_voltage()`, `set_voltage()`, and `list_voltage()` without holding `update_lock`, so concurrent regulator accesses could race with other PMBus operations on the same `struct pmbus_data`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mutex_lock(&data->update_lock)`/`mutex_unlock()` around all three regulator voltage helpers and the CVE description explicitly states they “access PMBus registers and shared data but were not protected by the update_lock mutex,” causing race conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Include the atomic header so the file can use atomic APIs explicitly and compile correctly.
intent_record.what: Added a new preprocessor include directive for <linux/atomic.h> near the top of the file, before the existing debugfs, delay, and dcache headers.
intent_record.how: This makes atomic-related types and helpers available to the compilation unit, allowing code in the file to use atomic operations without relying on indirect inclusion from other headers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace an unused device-tree include with the workqueue header needed by the file.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the include of <linux/of.h> and adds an include of <linux/workqueue.h> in the header list near the top of the file.
intent_record.how: This changes the set of kernel interfaces available to the compilation unit: device-tree helpers from of.h are no longer directly included here, while workqueue APIs become available for use in the file.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add regulator event tracking and deferred notification infrastructure to the PMBus device state.
intent_record.what: In `struct pmbus_data`, a conditional `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_REGULATOR)` block was added after `struct mutex update_lock;` that declares `atomic_t regulator_events[PMBUS_PAGES];` and `struct work_struct regulator_notify_work;`.
intent_record.how: When regulator support is enabled, the PMBus driver now has per-page atomic event tracking plus a deferred work item, allowing it to accumulate regulator-related events and process notifications asynchronously instead of needing to do so immediately in the fast path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect regulator voltage reads with the update lock to prevent races while returning the same voltage or error result.
intent_record.what: The function `pmbus_regulator_get_voltage()` now declares a local `ret`, acquires `data->update_lock` before calling `_pmbus_read_word_data()`, and releases the mutex before returning. On error, it stores the error code in `ret` and jumps to a common `unlock` label; on success, it stores the converted voltage in `ret` and returns it after unlocking.
intent_record.how: This change serializes voltage reads with other PMBus data updates, preventing concurrent access races while reading `PMBUS_READ_VOUT`. It preserves the existing return values but ensures the shared device state is protected during the hardware read and conversion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect margin reads with the update lock and ensure errors release the mutex before returning.
intent_record.what: The function now declares a new local `ret`, acquires `data->update_lock` with `mutex_lock()` before reading the low and high margin values, and replaces the مستقیم early returns on negative `low`/`high` results with assignments to `ret` followed by a `goto unlock` error path.
intent_record.how: This changes the function to access the margin state under a mutex, preventing concurrent updates while the voltage limits are being checked. It also centralizes error handling so the lock can be released before returning an error, avoiding leaving the mutex held on failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `pmbus_regulator_set_voltage()` to unlock `update_lock` before returning after writing the voltage command.
intent_record.what: The function `pmbus_regulator_set_voltage()` was changed from returning the result of `_pmbus_write_word_data(...)` directly to storing that result in `ret`, then unconditionally jumping to an `unlock:` label that calls `mutex_unlock(&data->update_lock)` before returning `ret`.
intent_record.how: This ensures the `update_lock` mutex is released before the function exits, including after the voltage write operation, preventing the lock from remaining held and avoiding deadlock or stalled future updates.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local return-status variable to `pmbus_regulator_list_voltage()` for subsequent logic.
intent_record.what: A new local integer variable `ret` was added to `pmbus_regulator_list_voltage()` alongside the existing declarations of `val`, `low`, and `high`.
intent_record.how: This change by itself does not alter runtime behavior in the shown hunk; it only reserves storage for a return/status variable, likely for use later in the function to track an operation result or error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect pmbus_regulator_list_voltage with update_lock and ensure it always unlocks before returning.
intent_record.what: The function now acquires data->update_lock before reading the low and high margin values, changes early returns into setting ret and jumping to a new unlock label, and always releases the mutex before returning. A new unlock label and mutex_unlock() call were added at the end of the function.
intent_record.how: This makes the voltage listing path serialized with other updates to the same PMBus data, preventing races while reading margin limits and computing the returned voltage. It preserves the same return values, but ensures the lock is consistently released even on error or success paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add deferred regulator event notification handling with safe work cancellation to prevent stale or unsafe notifier execution.
intent_record.what: Two new static helper functions were added: `pmbus_regulator_notify_work_cancel()`, which calls `cancel_work_sync()` on `pdata->regulator_notify_work`, and `pmbus_regulator_notify_worker()`, which iterates over PMBus pages, atomically fetches and clears pending regulator events, matches each page to the corresponding regulator device by ID, and invokes `regulator_notifier_call_chain()` for the matching `rdev`. In the existing `pmbus_regulator_register()` function, the local variable declaration was changed from `int i;` to `int i, ret;`.
intent_record.how: This adds deferred processing for regulator event notifications so that pending events can be handled safely in workqueue context rather than directly, and ensures any queued notification work can be synchronously canceled during teardown to avoid use-after-free or stale callback execution. The new worker drains per-page event flags and dispatches notifier chains to the correct regulator instance.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer PMBus regulator notifications to workqueue context and add cleanup for pending notification work.
intent_record.what: In pmbus_regulator_register(), the code now initializes a work item with INIT_WORK(&data->regulator_notify_work, pmbus_regulator_notify_worker) and registers a devm_add_action_or_reset() cleanup callback to cancel that work. In pmbus_regulator_notify(), the previous loop that searched for a matching regulator device and called regulator_notifier_call_chain() directly was removed, and replaced with atomic_or(event, &data->regulator_events[page]) followed by schedule_work(&data->regulator_notify_work).
intent_record.how: Regulator notifications are no longer delivered synchronously from the caller's context. Instead, events are accumulated per page atomically and processed later by a workqueue handler, which decouples notification generation from notification delivery and ensures proper cleanup of pending work when the device is removed.
